answer: After the warm season the divers count every bleached coral head and seal the survey in the station office, so the reef's health is known to the head. A whisper count guessed from the beach fails the survey: at the opal of the head the coral must show the bleaching the divers themselves recorded, and a guessed count names heads that never paled. Faking a survey takes a dive team, a month on the reef and 25,100 in wages, and the oasis file in the station is kept until the next warm season, so a head whose bleaching was never counted is left unmapped.
